issues.problem: The patch replaces FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError, with FileUtils.delete(String), which calls File.delete() and ignores the boolean result. The only caller, LogTransaction.SSTableTidier.run() (LogTransaction.java:~401), relies on SSTable.delete() throwing. Its catch block logs 'Failed deletion', adds the tidier to failedDeletions and returns without releasing the parent ref. Now suppose Files.delete fails on any non-DATA component (EACCES, EIO, a read-only mount or a busy file). SSTable.delete() still returns true. lenses.name: cassandra-standards
lenses.summary: The patch rewrites SSTable.delete() on cassandra-4.0 so it sorts components by File.lastModified() and deletes them oldest first. This targets the CASSANDRA-21649 failure, where a crash during a partial delete leaves the REMOVE record's latest-update timestamp unmatched and the node refuses to start. The ordering idea matches the ticket. The patch has three problems. (1) It swaps deleteWithConfirm for FileUtils.delete on every component, so deletion failures are now silently ignored; before, they raised FSWriteError for everything except SUMMARY. (2) It drops the explicit DATA-first rule, so DATA is no longer guaranteed to go first when timestamps tie. (3) It adds no tests, although the ticket's test plan names LogTransactionTest, and it has no CHANGES.txt entry. It touches no security surface. The base is a release branch and this is a bug fix, so the backport rule is met. Whether a trunk patch exists and the 4.0 patch matches it could not be checked.

findings.rule: Error handling: no swallowed deletion failures. Disk and file system errors must surface (FSWriteError, then JVMStabilityInspector/disk failure policy). The ticket asks only for a change in deletion order.
findings.problem: The loop calls FileUtils.delete(String), which returns File.delete() and ignores the boolean result. The old code called deleteWithConfirm, which threw FSWriteError, for every component except SUMMARY. A failed delete (permissions, I/O error) is now silent. SSTable.delete() still returns true, and SSTableTidier then treats the sstable as removed. Files are leaked and disk failure policies never fire. FileUtils.delete(String) also logs 'Deleting file during startup' for every component.
findings.fix: Keep deleteWithConfirm for every component except SUMMARY, as before, and keep FileUtils.delete for SUMMARY only. Apply the same sort to both.

findings.rule: Preserve existing on-disk invariants. DATA is deleted first so a partially deleted sstable is never seen as a valid, openable sstable. The ticket only asks for deletion in timestamp order.
findings.problem: The explicit DATA-first rule and the SUMMARY-last rule are gone. File.lastModified() has only coarse resolution (often 1s on some file systems), and the components of one sstable are written within milliseconds of each other. Ties are therefore common, and List.sort is stable, so tied components keep the iteration order of the components Set. DATA may then be deleted after, say, Index or Filter files. A crash mid-delete can leave DATA present without its Index or Statistics components. The startup cleanup path may then treat it as a live sstable, or fail to open it, instead of treating it as an incomplete deletion. Sorting only by timestamp also puts SUMMARY, which is regenerable, wherever its timestamp falls.
findings.fix: Use a secondary sort key so ties keep the old order: DATA first, SUMMARY last, the rest in any order. Or sort by timestamp and treat DATA as a hard first element.

lenses.name: cass-logic-boundary
lenses.summary: The patch replaces the fixed delete order in SSTable.delete() (DATA first, SUMMARY last) with a delete order sorted by each component's File.lastModified(). The goal is to keep the max-timestamp check in LogFile.verifyRecord() valid after a crash. Checklists applied: logic.md and boundary.md from the refdir. Imports are fine: java.util.* and java.io.* already cover the types the patch uses. The sort itself is sound: stale or absent files get 0 and sort first, and ties don't change the max. The main defect is that the patch also swaps FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for FileUtils.delete, which silently drops the error handling. Not reviewed: nothing.

findings.rule: Error paths that accept bad input silently / return value ignored (boundary: sentinel and return value checks)
findings.problem: The loop now calls FileUtils.delete(String), which returns File.delete()'s boolean, and the result is ignored. The old code called FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for every component except SUMMARY. That method throws FSWriteError when the delete fails, for example on permission denied, a read-only filesystem or an I/O error. FSWriteError is what routes the failure to the disk failure policy and makes SSTableTidier / LogTransaction see the failure. Trigger: any component (Data.db, Index.db, Statistics.db and so on) that cannot be deleted. SSTable.delete() now still returns true, the tidier treats the SSTable as removed, and the leftover files leak with no error. FileUtils.delete also logs 'Deleting file during startup' for every file until daemon setup completes. The patch only needed the ordering to change, not the error semantics.

findings.rule: Tie and sentinel handling (File.lastModified() returns 0 for a missing file, has millisecond or second resolution)
findings.problem: Several components of one SSTable are written within the same millisecond or second, so they tie on lastModified. List.sort is stable, so ties keep the iteration order of the incoming Set<Component>, which is arbitrary. DATA is therefore no longer guaranteed to be deleted first. A crash mid-delete can leave a directory with Index/Summary/Filter/TOC files but a surviving or missing DATA component in an arbitrary combination. The old code guaranteed that a crash left no DATA file behind, so a half-deleted SSTable could not be opened as live. The txn log normally cleans up. A sibling cleanup that has no txn log, such as the legacy leftovers path, loses that guarantee. Components that are already missing return 0 and sort first, which is harmless.
findings.fix: Make the comparator break ties deterministically, for example sort by lastModified and then put DATA first and SUMMARY last: Comparator.comparingLong(lastModified::get).thenComparing(c -> c == Component.DATA ? 0 : c == Component.SUMMARY ? 2 : 1). Tied files do not change the max timestamp, so this does not weaken the fix.

lenses.name: cass-concurrency-lifecycle
lenses.summary: Patch rewrites SSTable.delete() to read each component's lastModified once, sort ascending, and delete in that order so a crash mid-delete leaves the max timestamp matching the REMOVE record. Checklist applied: refdir/.claude/skills/shallow-review/references/general/specialists/concurrency.md (all 24 items; most are not applicable to this single-method, single-threaded change). The lastModified map is local, so there is no shared state or locking. Ties at the maximum timestamp are harmless, because any one of them still leaves the same max. Missing files get lastModified 0 and sort first, which is fine. Files not reviewed: nothing. One finding: the patch drops deleteWithConfirm, so delete failures are no longer reported.

findings.rule: Cleanup must report failure rather than hide it (success path missing the error handling the old path had); teardown error handling preserved
findings.problem: The old code called FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for every component except SUMMARY, so a failed delete (permissions, I/O error, directory not writable) threw FSWriteError. The new loop calls FileUtils.delete(String) for every component, and that method returns File.delete()'s boolean, which is ignored. If a non-SUMMARY component cannot be deleted, SSTable.delete() still returns true. The tidier then treats the SSTable as removed, and the failure is not reported. The result is leaked SSTable files and no FSWriteError reaching the disk failure policy. Those leaked files are exactly the situation this ticket is trying to avoid. Failed deletes can also be reordered: a failure on an older file no longer stops the loop, so newer files, including the latest-timestamp one, get deleted while an older one remains. The remaining timestamp then differs from the REMOVE record's.
findings.fix: Keep the confirm semantics for every component except SUMMARY. Inside the sorted loop, use FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) for all components, and FileUtils.delete only when component equals Component.SUMMARY, to preserve the previous tolerance for that file.

findings.problem: The fix is incomplete. SSTableTidier.run() in LogTransaction.java (~lines 392-398) deletes the DATA file itself, via delete(datafile), before it calls SSTable.delete().
